title: Research: dispositions for stayturgid issue #151's untracked Termux-family apps
description:
GitHub issue: https://github.com/djbclark/stayturgid/issues/151

SCOPE — RESEARCH/RECOMMENDATION ONLY, NOT A CODE-CHANGE TASK. Do not modify ansible_collections/stayturgid/android_common/roles/bootstrap_apks/ or any other config. Do not run any commands against actual fleet devices (adb/ssh/etc) — desk research and reasoning about existing issue content only, unless read-only device inspection is unambiguously safe and non-disruptive. Deliverable is a recommendation posted as a GitHub issue comment. Do not close the issue.

Context: PR #194 already landed com.termux.x11 pinning (the actively-used one). This issue's remaining, still-open scope is the other 7 untracked Termux-family/third-party packages found on fleet devices via live pm list packages (p7a, 2026-07-30):
- com.termux.tasker (0.9.0), com.termux.styling (0.32.1), com.termux.window (0.17.0), com.termux.widget (0.15.0) — official Termux-family, no version pin/checksum/update coverage currently.
- io.github.swiftstagrime.termuxrunner (1.7.2), com.gardockt.termuxterminalwidget (1.3), com.maazm7d.termuxhub (3.2.4) — third-party, unclear provenance (installer=null on all of them, likely Obtainium leftover).

Open questions to research and answer with a recommendation (not just present tradeoffs):
- For each of the 3 third-party apps: what does the app actually do, is it still useful/needed, any red flags (abandoned, security concerns, better alternatives)? Recommend keep-and-lock vs remove for each.
- Is com.termux.window distinct from com.termux.x11 in a way that matters, or does one supersede the other? (Both were found installed simultaneously.)
- For whichever apps are recommended to keep: sketch what a bootstrap_apks lock entry would need (gh_repo/gh_tag/gh_pattern/checksum, resign:true if unsigned) — don't write the actual ansible changes, just specify what's needed so a follow-up implementation task can act on it directly.
- The issue also asks that whatever solution is chosen make it easy to add future Termux companion apps, not just backfill the current gap — note any structural suggestion for that, but don't implement it.

Post findings as a comment on https://github.com/djbclark/stayturgid/issues/151.

title: Research: should AI-context-pack generation (Repomix or alternative) be wired into the ops release mechanism?
description:
GitHub issue: https://github.com/djbclark/site-djbclark/issues/35

Summary: git ls-files+tiktoken / repomix token counts gathered across all 3 repos (stayturgid ~1.05-1.16M, site-djbclark ~0.2M, site-private ~0.07-0.08M tokens). Proposal: wire an AI-context-pack generator (Repomix or alternative) into just ops-release-check/ops-release-deploy so each tagged ops-vX.Y.Z release ships a versioned context snapshot as a release asset.

Open questions to resolve (this is a RESEARCH task — produce a recommendation, not a release-mechanism code change, unless the recommendation is to implement and that's confirmed separately):
- Release-time trigger vs CI-on-merge-to-master vs on-demand only?
- One pack per repo or one combined pack for the 3-repo suite?
- Plain vs --compress (or both)?
- Artifact location: GitHub Release asset vs committed to repo vs generate-on-demand only?
- Should pack-generation failure block a release, or just log/warn?
- Also evaluate alternatives to Repomix: gitingest, code2prompt, yek, Aider's repo-map, MCP-based context servers (LLM Context, Repo Prompt) — issue notes we're mostly targeting Claude Code sessions which already have on-demand file-reading/search tools, so worth questioning whether a static full-repo pack is even the right primitive.
- Flag risk of staleness, secret/vault-file leakage, and release-artifact storage bloat.

The issue includes a ready-to-paste second-opinion prompt for a fresh/differently-sourced AI session — see the GitHub issue body for the exact text if useful.

Deliverable: post findings/recommendation back as a comment on https://github.com/djbclark/site-djbclark/issues/35 (do not close the issue without explicit confirmation).
close_reason: Posted research findings/recommendation as comment on issue #35: recommend against wiring context-pack generation into the release mechanism (decoupled, on-demand instead); evaluated Repomix/gitingest/code2prompt/yek/Aider repo-map/MCP context servers; flagged staleness/secret/storage risks
